title: Chemical modification and zinc coordination enhance the antioxidant activity of Gastrodia elata polysaccharides: a structure–activity relationship approach
content:
Abstract

Background

The functional properties of Gastrodia elata polysaccharides (GEP) are closely related to their structural characteristics. This study investigated the effects of sulfation, acetylation, and zinc ion (Zn2+) coordination on GEP structure and antioxidant activity.

Results

Sulfated GEP (S-GEP) and acetylated GEP (Ac-GEP) were prepared and subsequently coordinated with Zn2+. Structural analyses revealed that chemical modification altered functional groups and chain organization, while Zn2+ coordination induced further structural reorganization. All modifications enhanced antioxidant activity, with Ac-Zn-GEP exhibiting the highest DPPH (2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl) and hydroxyl radical scavenging rates (69.09% and 69.46%, respectively, at 10 mg/mL). Ac-Zn-GEP also showed the strongest cytoprotective effect against hydrogen peroxide-induced oxidative stress, accompanied by decreased malondialdehyde levels and increased total antioxidant capacity.

Conclusion

Acetylation combined with Zn2+ coordination effectively improved the structural and antioxidant properties of GEP, providing insights into the structure–activity relationships of polysaccharide–metal complexes. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
